neighbours.label: a word-initial ' e'/'E' split off as its own token at the start of a rare word (e|bbing, e|aves, e|ases)
fire: By evening the floodwater was finally ebbed back to the river.
The children sat on the porch, eavesdropping on the adults.
Pigeons nested under the eaves of the old barn.
A cup of tea often eases a sore throat.
The painter set his easel by the window.
The villagers eked out a living from the thin soil.
The fog lifted and the wind turned easterly at noon.
The old house felt eerily silent after the guests left.
quiet: By evening the floodwater was finally drained back to the river.
The children sat on the porch, listening to the adults.
Pigeons nested under the gutters of the old barn.
A cup of tea often soothes a sore throat.
The painter set his canvas by the window.
The villagers scraped out a living from the thin soil.
The fog lifted and the wind turned northerly at noon.
The old house felt strangely silent after the guests left.

notes: Card: ' e' x7, 'E'/' E'/Cyrillic ' е' x9; examples easterly, ebbing, eaves, eases. Probe: ebbing 1.08, eaves 0.71, eases 0.42, easterly 0.41. Near misses: same frames with rare words starting with other letters.
